captions.text: 1970: the capital is Awka.
1970: Fiji is independent.
1970: the Boundary Treaty (signed 23 November 1970, in force 18 April 1972).

The Egypt dossier cuts the Halaib Triangle out of Egypt from 1971 (and the United Arab Republic's shape holds it in 1970) but no dossier gives it to Sudan, so 86 cells stay owned by nobody until 1994.
The 1970 anchor leaves seven Sakhalin and Kuril cells with Japan.
15 January 1970: Biafra surrenders.
15 January 1970: Biafra ends and Nigeria is reunited.
23 February 1970: Guyana becomes a republic.
2 March 1970: Rhodesia declares itself a republic.
1970: the PAVN takes the Cambodian north-east.
1970: North Vietnam takes the north-east.

1970: South Vietnamese and US forces enter eastern Cambodia (the Cambodian campaign, 29 April to 22 July): ARVN at the Parrot's Beak on 30 April, US forces at the Fishhook on 1 May (withdrawn by 30 June).
24 April 1970: the Gambia becomes a republic within the Commonwealth.
April 1970: the Cambodian campaign.

1 May 1970: 'elements of SVN PAVN units (28th and 24A regiments) joined with North Vietnamese Army and Pathet Lao to seize Attapeu'; the Ho Chi Minh trail page also has Attapeu and Salavan 'seized by the PAVN during 1970'.
1970: PAVN and the Pathet Lao seize Attapeu (1 May): 'PAVN units (28th and 24A regiments) joined the NVA and Pathet Lao to seize Attapeu'.
1970: the campaign ends (22 July) with the withdrawal of ARVN and US forces; ARVN's zone was later reduced to 'a depth of 10-15 km' (mid-1971).
July 1970: the attacks end ('April-July 1970') and the South Vietnamese and US forces withdraw; the exact day (22 July) is the Cambodia dossier's, not this page's.
9 August 1970: Qaboos proclaims the Sultanate of Oman.
1970: Fiji becomes independent from the United Kingdom as the Dominion of Fiji.
1970: Fiji becomes independent on 10 October 1970 ('With this compromise, Fiji became independent on 10 October 1970'), a Dominion under the Crown (oc-02-b's republic-of-fiji dossier carries it).

1970: the monarchy is abolished and the Khmer Republic proclaimed (9 October) by Lon Nol, who had overthrown Sihanouk on 18 March 1970; same state, same colour (rule 2). The Kingdom page: 'the monarchy was abolished in a coup on 9 October 1970'.
November 1970: Hafez al-Assad takes power.
The Golan cells are owned by nobody in the 1970 anchor, so Israel's own 1967 occupation_start (recorded by Israel, over land Syria does not hold) is read the wrong way round and marks nothing.
30 November 1970: the state becomes the People's Democratic Republic of Yemen.
1 December 1970: the civil war ends.
Israel holds the Golan Heights taken from Syria on 9-10 June 1967 through the 1970s (1974: the disengagement 'left almost all the Heights in Israeli hands'; 14 December 1981: the Golan Heights Law).
1 December 1970: the royalist war ends.
1971: Egypt takes the name Arab Republic of Egypt.
Carried over from the predecessor dossier: Israel has held the Sinai since the Six-Day War of June 1967 ('Israel occupied the entire Sinai Peninsula, and Gaza Strip from Egypt').
1971: Bahrain is independent.
1971: the Trucial States form the Federation of Arab Emirates.
1971: Qatar is independent.
1971: the capital moves from Belize City to Belmopan.
1971: Mobutu renames the country the Republic of Zaire.
1971: the Pathet Lao and PAVN 'captured the Bolaven Plateau' (Laotian Civil War page, placed in 1971); the Ho Chi Minh trail page has 'During 1971 PAVN took Paksong and advanced to Pakse'.
1971: the Bolaven Plateau falls.
1971: Bahrain's British tie ends (page silent on Bahrain itself).
26 March 1971: Bangladesh proclaims independence.
1971: the Bangladesh Liberation War.
25 March 1971: Pakistan's army strikes East Pakistan.
1971-04-19: Sierra Leone becomes a republic.
15 August 1971: Bahrain becomes independent.
August 1971: the protectorate ends.
3 September 1971: Qatar becomes independent.
3 September 1971: the protectorate ends in independence.
September 1971: Egypt becomes the Arab Republic of Egypt.
27 October 1971: Mobutu renames the country the Republic of Zaire.
1971: the Swan Islands pass to Honduras.
30 November 1971: Iran seizes the Tunbs and Abu Musa.
29-30 November 1971: Iran seizes the Tunbs and Abu Musa.
2 December 1971: six emirates form the United Arab Emirates.
1971: the surrender at Dhaka.
1971: East Pakistan becomes Bangladesh.
16 December 1971: Pakistan surrenders.
16 December 1971: East Pakistan becomes Bangladesh.
December 1971: the seat of government moves from Meherpur to Dhaka.
3 December 1971: India enters the war in East Pakistan.
16 December 1971: Pakistan surrenders in Dhaka.
1 December 1971: British protection ends.
2 December 1971: six Trucial States form the United Arab Emirates.
1 December 1971: the Trucial treaties end and the Emirates become the United Arab Emirates.

East Pakistan, proclaimed as the sovereign state of Bangladesh on 26 March 1971: 'independence of East Pakistan as the sovereign state of Bangladesh'; Pakistan held it until its surrender on 16 December 1971
the same state in its first Zaire years: the shape of the Democratic Republic of the Congo row alive in 1971, unchanged by the renaming of 27 October 1971
1972: Cliopatria's Arab Socialist Ba'ath Party row ends and its 'Syria' row begins in 1973 over the same cells.
1972: the PAVN withdraws from the north-east.
1972: Okinawa returns to Japan.

1972: North Vietnamese forces 'gradually and deliberately scaled back their presence' in Cambodia, leaving the insurgents (CPNLAF, the Khmer Rouge) in the north-east; the Civil War page says the combat was handed to the insurgents ('Khmerization') as their strength reached 35-40,000.
1972: the north-east passes to the Khmer Rouge and its fighting with the Republic.
1972: North Yemen seizes Kamaran.
1972: Ras al-Khaimah joins the federation.

1972: the PAVN takes Lộc Ninh on 7 April, in the Easter Offensive ('before collapsing under the attack on 7 April'); the page says Lộc Ninh or An Lộc 'would be proclaimed as the capital of the Provisional Revolutionary Government', and the PRG page lists Lộc Ninh as capital 1972-73.
1972: the PRG capital moves from Tây Ninh to Lộc Ninh (PRG infobox: Lộc Ninh 1972-1973).
1972: Quảng Trị City falls to the PAVN on 2 May; the advance was 'halted on 5 May at the Mỹ Chánh Line'.
20 May 1972: the federation is abolished and the country becomes the United Republic of Cameroon.
22 May 1972: the Dominion becomes a republic.
15 May 1972: 'control of Okinawa was given back to Japan on 15 May 1972'.
1972, 15 May: the page says 'control of Okinawa was given back to Japan on 15 May 1972'.
1972: the ARVN retakes Quảng Trị, the Citadel 'finally taken on 16 September', and 'the majority of Quang Tri province'; the north-west around Cam Lộ stays PAVN/PRG.

1973: Cliopatria's 'Syria' row begins over the cells of its Arab Socialist Ba'ath Party row; the Syrian Arab Republic has stood since the end of the French mandate ('17 April 1946', infobox) and this is a row boundary, not a founding.
1973: the Bahamas are independent.
1973: Libya occupies and annexes the Aouzou Strip of northern Chad.
1973: the PRG capital moves to Cam Lộ in Quảng Trị (PRG infobox: Cam Lộ 1973-1975).
1973: Libya occupies the Aouzou Strip.

Carried over from the predecessor dossier: Israel has held the Golan Heights since June 1967 ('the Israel Defense Forces captured the Golan Heights on [9-10 June]'; 1,070 km2 of the Heights proper and 100 km2 of the Hermon slopes).
1973: the Paris Peace Accords (27 January) leave the PRG and the PAVN in their zones.
1973: the Paris Peace Accords (27 January) leave the communist forces in their zones.
1 June 1973: British Honduras is renamed Belize.

1973: Papadopoulos 'abolished the monarchy and declared Greece a republic' on 1 June (infobox 'Republic declared: 1 June 1973'; the 29 July 1973 referendum was 'not recognised by the political parties').
10 July 1973: the Bahamas becomes independent.
17 July 1973: Daoud Khan overthrows the king and proclaims the Republic of Afghanistan.
17 July 1973: Daoud Khan overthrows the monarchy.
24 September 1973: the PAIGC's People's National Assembly declares the independence of the Republic of Guinea-Bissau.
September 1973: Portuguese forces still hold the cities.
6 October 1973: Egypt crosses the Suez Canal.
6 October 1973: Israel's hold on the east bank of the canal ends.
25 October 1973: the war ends.
6 October 1973: Egypt crosses the Suez Canal.
25 October 1973: Israel holds the west bank.

After the October 1973 war Israel still held the Sinai: the Egypt ledger's occupation_end events (6 Oct 1973, 1974, 1975) each close the whole Israeli occupation, though they release only the canal strip.
6 October 1973: Syria attacks on the Golan.
25 October 1973: the war ends.
25 October 1973: on the Golan front 'Israeli forces held 500 km2 of the Syrian Bashan region of the Golan Heights' at the ceasefire (infobox).
6 October 1973: Syria and Egypt attack Israel and the Golan front opens.
25 October 1973: the fighting ends.
The Ba'ath Party row of Syria ends in 1972 and 'syria' takes over the same cells in 1973, which closes the occupation of the previous entry.
the 1969 shape without Fiji and the Bahamas (independent 1973)
the archipelago of 'some 700 islands and 2,400 cays': the Cliopatria polygon plus the whole country, so that cays the polygon misses are not dropped
shape unchanged; the years change: the regime fell on 24 July 1974, so the shape holds for 1973-1974 only and 1975 belongs to the Third Hellenic Republic
3.18 M km2 for 1973-1975, 3.287 M km2 in the infobox (ratio 0.97; the infobox lists 'Territory claimed but not controlled').
2,060,583 km2: one cell differs from 1972 (28.68E, -30.13 swaps with 28.97E, -30.01).
314.1 k km2 against the infobox 315,331 km2 for 2020s Oman (ratio 1.00): the modern outline, which includes Dhofar and Musandam.
887,273 km2, 0.1% above 1967 and 0.1% above 1976: cartographic noise, no event on any page opened explains it. Infobox 947,303 km2 (ratio 0.94).
1974: Israel gives up the ground it took in 1973.

The dossier's 1974 occupation_end (the west bank of the canal) closes the pair's whole occupation again; the Sinai east of the canal strip stayed Israeli until 1982 ('In 1982, as a result of the Egypt-Israel peace treaty of 1979, Israel withdrew from all of the Sinai Peninsula').
1974: Grenada is independent.
1974: Niue becomes self-governing, 'as did Niue from 1974', in free association with New Zealand.
1974: Kachchatheevu passes to Sri Lanka.
1974: Kachchatheevu is ceded to Sri Lanka.
1974: Quneitra returns to Syrian civil administration.
1974: Quneitra returns to Syria.
1974: the Socialist Republic of the Union of Burma.
1974: China seizes the Paracels from South Vietnam.
7 February 1974: Grenada becomes independent.
7 February 1974: independence under Eric Gairy; same state, same land.
1974: the Carnation Revolution of 25 April 1974, a coup by the Armed Forces Movement, 'led to the end of the Estado Novo'; the Third Portuguese Republic begins the same day.
1974: the junta falls and the Third Hellenic Republic begins on 24 July.
1974: the junta falls on 24 July.
1974: the Turkish army lands at Kyrenia on 20 July, five days after the Greek junta's coup against Makarios (15 July).
20 July 1974: Turkey invades Cyprus.
1974: the Turkish invasion leaves the north under a Turkish Cypriot administration.
1974: Guinea-Bissau.
1974: fighting ends in August with Turkey holding the north.
August 1974: the second operation ends in the Turkish zone.
1974: Turkey holds the northern 36 % of the island.
1974: Turkey holds northern Cyprus.
12 September 1974: the Derg deposes Haile Selassie.
10 September 1974: Portugal grants full independence.

1974: Niue becomes self-governing in free association with New Zealand: infobox 'Self-government in free association with New Zealand: 19 October 1974'; the page also says Niue has been self-governing 'since 3 September 1974, when the people endorsed the Constitution in a plebiscite'.
1974: Malta becomes a republic on 13 December.
the Greek state as the Third Hellenic Republic from the fall of the junta, unchanged in outline from the 1976 shape

the northern four-elevenths of Cyprus (about 36%) held by Turkish forces after the second phase of the invasion in August 1974, the ground of the Autonomous Turkish Cypriot Administration and then the Turkish Federated State of Cyprus
1975: Israel pulls back from the canal and it reopens.

The 1975 occupation_end (Israel leaves the canal area, 'The canal was reopened in 1975') closes the pair's whole occupation; the rest of the Sinai stays Israeli to 1982 (the 1979 treaty: 'Israel agreed to withdraw from the entirety of the Sinai Peninsula').
1975: the Pegu Yoma base falls.
1975: with the Pegu Yoma base gone the contest in Pegu Region ends.
1975: the headquarters is at Panghsang by November 1978 and 'remained there until 1989'; the page does not date the move, so 1975 is a bridging judgment (page silent).
1975: Angola becomes a People's Republic ('Angola and Mozambique became People's Republics in 1975'); the pages opened give no day.
1975: Mozambique becomes a People's Republic; the pages opened give no day.
1975: Cape Verde 'independence in 1975' (Carnation Revolution page; no day).
1975: Sao Tome and Principe 'independence in 1975' (Carnation Revolution page; no day).
1975: Iraq cedes the eastern bank of the Shatt al-Arab to Iran under the Algiers Agreement.
1975: Manerplaw is established; 'Manerplaw was established in 1975' (Manerplaw page) and the KNU headquarters is there 'until 1995' (KNU infobox).
1975: the capital moves from Zomba to Lilongwe.
1975: Phước Long falls on 6 January, the first provincial capital the PAVN holds.

13 February 1975: Turkey declares the occupied area a 'Federated Turkish State', the forerunner of the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus (independence declared in 1983, 'Turkey is the only country that recognises it'). The relation runs to 2024.
1975: the Turkish Federated State of Cyprus is declared on 13 February.

13 February 1975: 'Turkey declared the occupied areas of the Republic of Cyprus to be a "Federated Turkish State"' (reopened 2026-11-01); the same page says of the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus 'Turkey is the only country that recognises it'.
March 1975: the monarchy is abolished.

1975: Buôn Ma Thuột falls on 18 March and Darlac Province with it. [Reviewer se-04-x: confidence 3 to 2; the Ho Chi Minh campaign page dates the city ('capturing the city of Buôn Ma Thuột on 18 March') but does not name the province.]
1975: the Central Highlands are abandoned in mid-March: 'Pleiku and Kon Tum were to be abandoned'.
1975: Huế falls by the end of March (the page gives no day).
1975: Đà Nẵng falls on 29 March.
1975: the Khmer Rouge capture Phnom Penh (17 April) and empty the city.
1975: Saigon falls (30 April).
1975: the zones merge into the conquest of South Vietnam (30 April, below).
1975: the Khmer Rouge hold the country from the fall of the capital (17 April).
1975: the war ends on 17 April, when Phnom Penh surrendered to the Khmer Rouge.
1975: Phnom Penh falls to the Khmer Rouge (17 April), after Lon Nol resigned and left on 1 April; the last Republic-held area, the Preah Vihear temple, falls on 22 May.
1975: South Vietnam surrenders on 30 April.
1975: the PRG enters Saigon: 'the PRG moved into government offices there' after 30 April (the PRG page lists Saigon-Gia Dinh 1975-1976).
1975: the war ends with the surrender of 30 April; the original contest zone passes wholly to the PRG.
30 April 1975: the zones merge into the conquest of the whole Republic.
30 April 1975: the war ends with 'Communist forces overran Saigon on 30 April 1975'; the contested land becomes the PRG's and Hanoi's.
30 April 1975: Saigon falls and the Republic of Vietnam ends.
May 1975: the Khmer Rouge raid Vietnamese islands.
16 May 1975: the Kingdom of Sikkim ends in merger with India (Kingdom page: 'The merger with India took effect on 16 May 1975'), after a referendum on the monarchy.
16 May 1975: Sikkim ends its protectorate status by merging with India.
16 May 1975: Sikkim becomes India's 22nd state.
25 June 1975: Mozambique becomes independent from Portugal as the People's Republic of Mozambique.
25 June 1975: Mozambique becomes independent.
1975: Cape Verde becomes independent from Portugal.
1975: São Tomé and Príncipe becomes independent from Portugal.
1975: the Comoros leave France.
August 1975: the island dispute ends.
1975: Papua New Guinea becomes independent from Australia.
1975: Papua New Guinea becomes independent from Australia.

1975: the Ellice Islands separate from the Gilbert Islands as the Crown colony of Tuvalu: 'The Tuvaluan Order 1975, which took effect on 1 October 1975'; the joint colony 'legally ceased to exist on 1 October 1975' and 'separate administrations followed on 1 January 1976' after the 1974 referendum.
1975: the Ellice Islands separate (1 October 1975); the colony is known as the Gilbert Islands until independence in 1979.

1975: the Ellice Islands separate from the Gilbert Islands: 'On 1 October 1975, legal separation from the Gilbert Islands (now Kiribati), took place'; 'Tuvalu became an independent constitutional monarchy ...
1975: Fretilin declares East Timor independent at Dili (28 November).
1975: Angola becomes independent from Portugal.
25 November 1975: Suriname becomes independent from the Netherlands.
1975: UNITA sets up a rival government at Huambo.
1975 (25 November): independence.
14 November 1975: Spain agrees to leave the Sahara.
20 November 1975: Franco dies and the regime ends.
November 1975: the monarchy is restored.
6 November 1975: the Green March.
1975: South African columns hold the south and the Benguela coast.
1975: the civil war opens over the highlands.
1975: Huambo passes to the FNLA-UNITA government.
1975 November 11: independence.
28 November 1975: the colony ends.
30 November 1975: Dahomey is renamed Benin ('after the Bight of Benin'), and a self-described Marxist-Leninist People's Republic of Benin 'existed between 1975 and 1990'.
1975: the fight for the highlands opens.
1975: the Pathet Lao overthrow the royalist government and proclaim the Lao People's Democratic Republic (2 December).

1975: the strip passes to the Pathet Lao state with the end of the Kingdom of Laos: Pathet Lao forces took Vientiane on 23 August 1975 and the Lao People's Democratic Republic was proclaimed on 2 December 1975.

2 December 1975: the Laotian Civil War 'was officially declared over' and the Lao People's Democratic Republic was proclaimed, so Attapeu passes to the Pathet Lao state; mirrors kingdom-of-laos /ledger/11.

2 December 1975: the Laotian Civil War 'was officially declared over' and the Lao People's Democratic Republic was proclaimed, so the Bolaven Plateau passes to the Pathet Lao state; mirrors kingdom-of-laos /ledger/12.
7 December 1975: Indonesia invades.
1975: Fretilin 'unilaterally declared the colony's independence' on 28 November 1975 after a UDT coup in August; on 7 December 1975 'the Indonesian Armed Forces launched an invasion of East Timor'.
1975: the monarchy ends and the Pathet Lao rules the whole country (2 December).
1975: the Plain of Jars passes to the Pathet Lao with the rest of the country (2 December).
1975: the strip ends as Vietnamese-occupied land when the Pathet Lao takes the state (2 December); the Pathet Lao and Hanoi remained allied.
1975: Attapeu passes to the Pathet Lao state (2 December).
1975: the Bolaven Plateau passes to the Pathet Lao state (2 December).
1975: the Kingdom ends (2 December): 'It survived until 2 December 1975'.
1975: the First Republic gives way to the Marxist-Leninist Second Republic under Didier Ratsiraka.
December 1975: Mauritanian troops take Tichla and La Guera.
1975: the Pathet Lao rules the whole country (2 December).
1975: the Plain of Jars passes to the new state.
1975: the Pathet Lao takes the state (23 August Vientiane; 2 December the monarchy abolished and the Lao People's Democratic Republic proclaimed with Souphanouvong as President).
1975: the movement becomes the state, the Lao People's Democratic Republic (Cliopatria's Communist Laos row, from 1976).
1975: Indonesia invades East Timor (7 December), nine days after Fretilin declared independence on 28 November; Batugade fell on 8 October and Balibo on about 16 October.
December 1975: 'once the campaign was declared over in December 1975', the remaining PFLOAG fighters surrendered (the Oman page: 'finally put down in 1976').
the country at independence, 25 June 1975: the same outline as Cliopatria's 1976 Mozambique shape
new keyframe, years only: the shape of Cliopatria's 1976 row (Angola with Cabinda) holds from independence on 11 November 1975
the ten islands of Cape Verde ('about 4,033 square kilometres'), without the Comoros that Cliopatria's row also holds; new keyframe: independence on 5 July 1975, Cliopatria's row starts in 1976
the 1976 shape unchanged, carried back to independence: 'On 25 November 1975, it became independent following negotiations with the Dutch government'
new keyframe, years only: the shape of Cliopatria's 1976 row holds from independence on 12 July 1975
1976: Mauritania annexes the southern part of Western Sahara.
1976: Spain leaves and Morocco and Mauritania annex the territory.
27 February 1976: the Polisario proclaims the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic at Bir Lehlu and Morocco holds most of the territory.
1976: Morocco takes the north.
1976: Mauritania takes the south of Western Sahara.
1976: the constitution of Democratic Kampuchea is promulgated (5 January); the Khmer Rouge 'abolished the Royal Government of National Union of Kampuchea (GRUNK; established in 1970)'.
1976 (27 February): the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic is proclaimed at Bir Lehlou.
1976: the MPLA takes Huambo back.

1976: the Polisario war against Morocco, begun on 31 October 1975 (infobox '31 October 1975 - 6 September 1991'; Moroccan troops reached El Aaiun on 11 December 1975), continues under the new republic.
1976: the war against Mauritania.

The SADR keyframe takes the Laayoune-Boujdour and Oued el Dahab units and the Free Zone but not the Smara part of the Saguia el-Hamra, which the gazetteer files under Guelmim - Es-Semara; the 128 Smara cells stay owned by nobody from the Spanish withdrawal.
Seam sm-08, replacing events/4 (which now moves nothing).
Seam sm-08.
1976: the MPLA takes Huambo back.
1976: 'Morocco took over the Saguia El Hamra and the northern two-thirds of the territory' (Western Sahara War page; 'Morocco controls approximately 80% of the territory').
1976: South Africa withdraws from Angola.
1976: the Third Republic's Constitution takes effect on 25 April.
Seam sm-08.
Seam sm-08.
Seam sm-08.
31 May 1976: the Syrian army enters Lebanon.
31 May 1976: the Syrian army enters Lebanon.
1976: Seychelles becomes independent from the United Kingdom as a republic.
29 June 1976: the Seychelles become independent.
29 June 1976: with the Seychelles, the last of Britain's remaining African colonies in this set becomes independent.
1976: Aldabra, Farquhar and Desroches return to Seychelles.
1976: North and South Vietnam are united as the Socialist Republic of Vietnam (2 July).
1976: North and South unite as the Socialist Republic of Vietnam (2 July); the PRG page: the two 'constitutionally merged to form the current Socialist Republic of Vietnam'.
17 July 1976: Indonesia annexes East Timor.
1976: East Timor passes to Indonesia (17 July).
1976: Indonesia 'formally annexed East Timor, declaring it as its 27th province' on 17 July 1976; the UN did not recognise it and kept Portugal as the Administering Power.
1976: Portuguese Timor passes to Indonesian control; de jure Portugal remained the Administering Power in the UN's view.
1976: the PRG merges with the north on 2 July.
1976: the PRG ends and its land is the Socialist Republic of Vietnam's (PRG infobox: successor Socialist Republic of Vietnam; Viet Cong page: 'the PRG was dissolved' in July 1976).
1976: the contest ends in annexation (17 July); resistance continues, and the UN keeps Portugal as administering power (the infobox gives a de jure occupation to 20 May 2002).
1976: Indonesia annexes East Timor (17 July): 'Indonesia formally annexed East Timor as its 27th province'.
1 August 1976: the state becomes a republic within the Commonwealth.
1976: Transkei is declared independent on 26 October.
October 1976: Syria takes central Lebanon.
4 December 1976: Bokassa proclaims the Central African Empire.
28 December 1976: the People's Republic of Albania becomes the People's Socialist Republic.
all of Vietnam until the formal reunification of 2 July 1976
Portugal and Macau until the handover of 20 December 1999

for 1976 to 11 August 1979 the shape plus Tiris al-Gharbiyya, the southern third of Western Sahara that 'Mauritania took control of'; from August 1979 (1980 in yearly steps) the shape as drawn, because Mauritania 'withdrew all its forces' and Morocco annexed the area
483,568 km2 against the infobox 462,840 km2 (ratio 1.04), within coastal noise.
2,323,775 km2 to 2023, ratio 0.98 on the infobox; 300 km2 above the 1963 shape (noise).

The territory the Republic controls after 1974, the island south of the ceasefire line and the UN buffer zone, without the Sovereign Base Areas; the north (36.2 %) is claimed and occupied (occupation event), not lost in law
the Republic with East Timor, annexed as the 27th province on 17 July 1976; holds 1976-1998 only
337,618 km2 against the infobox's 331,344.82 km2 (ratio 1.02; the body also gives 331,210 and 331,699).
1975-1977: the fronts liberate nearly all of Eritrea.
2 March 1977: the General People's Congress proclaims the Socialist People's Libyan Arab Jamahiriya.
8 March 1977: Katangan rebels cross from Angola in the Shaba I invasion.
1977: the border war begins.
30 May 1977: the Mozambican Civil War begins (infobox 'Date: 30 May 1977 - 4 October 1992').
26 May 1977: the Shaba I invasion ends in Zairian victory.
1977: Djibouti becomes independent from France.
1977: the French Territory of the Afars and the Issas becomes independent as Djibouti on 27 June.
July 1977: Somalia invades the Ogaden.
The EPLF 1977 keyframe cuts Barentu out of the EPLF's land but nothing gives it to Ethiopia, so 21 cells stay owned by nobody.
1977: Somalia and the Western Somali Liberation Front invade the Ogaden.
1977: Khmer Rouge troops take Vietnamese border ground.

6 December 1977: Bophuthatswana is declared 'independent' under Lucas Mangope; only South Africa and Transkei recognised it. 'nominal independence on 6 December 1977' (infobox); 'The Status of Bophuthatswana Act 89 of 1977 granted Bophuthatswana "independence" with effect from 6 December 1977' (Bantustan page).
December 1977: Vietnam invades.
1977: Bophuthatswana is declared independent on 6 December.
new keyframe, years only: the shape of Cliopatria's 1979 row holds from independence on 27 June 1977
1978: Dominica is independent.
1978: the Solomon Islands are independent.
1978: the Derg counter-offensive forces the EPLF back to Nakfa.
January 1978: Hanoi withdraws.
February 1978: Libyan-backed rebels take Faya-Largeau and the north of Chad.
February 1978: Faya-Largeau falls and Libya-backed rebels take the north.
March 1978: Ethiopia regains the Ogaden.
1978: Ethiopia retakes the Ogaden.
March 1978: Israel invades south Lebanon.
1978: the PDPA proclaims the Democratic Republic of Afghanistan at Kabul.
27-28 April 1978: the Saur Revolution ends the republic.
May 1978: the Shaba II invasion and the Battle of Kolwezi.
May 1978: the Battle of Kolwezi is over within the month.
1978: the Solomon Islands become independent from the United Kingdom.
1978: the Solomon Islands become independent on 7 July 1978 (infobox 'Independence: 7 July 1978'; 'Self governance: 2 January 1976').
7 September 1978: the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka.
30 October 1978: Uganda invades the Kagera Salient of Tanzania.
1978-10: Uganda invades the Kagera Salient.
1978: Tuvalu becomes independent: 'On 1 October 1978, Tuvalu became fully independent as a sovereign state within the Commonwealth.'
3 November 1978: Dominica becomes independent.
December 1978: the frontier fighting gives way to the invasion.
25 December 1978: Vietnam invades Cambodia.
the whole country, as the Democratic Republic claimed it from 30 April 1978
Nakfa and the Sahel mountains, the EPLF's "liberated area" (given as a coordinate; the gazetteer lacks Nakfa)
1979: Saint Lucia is independent.
1979: the Soviet army enters Afghanistan.
1979: the Khmer Rouge fall back to the Thai border.
1979: the People's Republic of Kampuchea is proclaimed at Phnom Penh.
7 January 1979: the border war ends in the fall of the capital.
January 1979: the Khmer Rouge lose the country.
7 January 1979: Democratic Kampuchea falls.
Early January 1979: the last Ugandan troops leave Kagera.
7 January 1979: Phnom Penh falls.

1979: guerrilla war against the Vietnamese and the People's Republic of Kampuchea begins on the frontier; the KPNLF forms in October 1979 and 'operated from several refugee camps on the Thai-Cambodian border'.
1979: the Khmer Rouge hold out on the Thai frontier.
1979: Vietnamese occupation.
1979: ten years of Vietnamese occupation begin.
1979-01: the Kagera Salient is retaken.
20-21 January 1979: Tanzanian troops cross into Uganda.
11 February 1979: the Pahlavi dynasty falls.
22 February 1979: Saint Lucia becomes independent.
17 February 1979: China invades northern Vietnam.
13 March 1979: the New JEWEL Movement overthrows Gairy and sets up the People's Revolutionary Government under Maurice Bishop.
March 1979: the Kurdish rebellion begins as Kurdish forces seize towns in Iranian Kurdistan, before the republic is proclaimed on 1 April.
1979: the British leave on 31 March.
16 March 1979: the Chinese leave.
1979: Iran becomes an Islamic republic.
11 April 1979: Kampala falls and Amin's rule ends.
April 1979: Tanzanian forces hold Uganda behind the new UNLF government.
1979-04: Tanzanian forces hold Uganda after Kampala falls.
1979: Zimbabwe Rhodesia is born.
June 1979: the war ends.
1 June 1979: Rhodesia becomes Zimbabwe Rhodesia under Bishop Muzorewa.
1979-06: the war ends.

1979: the Gilbert Islands become independent as Kiribati: infobox 'Independence from the United Kingdom, Granted: 12 July 1979'; 'The Gilbert Islands gained independence as the Republic of Kiribati on 12 July 1979.'
1979: the Gilbert Islands become independent as Kiribati on 12 July 1979: 'The Gilbert Islands attained independence on 12 July 1979 under the name Kiribati.'
